import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Map 'is_fraud' to more descriptive labels for better clarity in the plot legend
df['Fraud Status'] = df['is_fraud'].map({0: 'Not Fraud', 1: 'Fraud'})

# Create the visualization
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Use a violinplot to show the distribution of transaction amounts,
# separated by transaction type and whether it's fraudulent.
# 'split=True' allows direct comparison of fraud vs. non-fraud distributions within each transaction type.
# 'inner="quartile"' shows the quartiles and median within each violin.
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', y='amount', hue='Fraud Status',
               split=True, inner='quartile',
               palette={'Not Fraud': 'skyblue', 'Fraud': 'salmon'})

# Set plot title and labels
plt.title('Distribution of Transaction Amount by Type and Fraud Status', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Adjust legend title and position
plt.legend(title='Fraud Status', loc='upper right', frameon=True, shadow=True)

# Add a grid for better readability of values on the y-axis
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Ensure layout is tight and save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
